reference: Bash type/help metadata and the documented bashsyslogd interface. Daemon file effects and routing require a future private socket/clock fixture; generic coreutils setup is not daemon operation parity.
coverage: Bash type metadata confirms bashsyslogd is registered as a builtin.
Bash help metadata contains documented run options and service behavior markers.
Deferred operational areas: local datagram routing and cleanup, configuration reload, UDP forwarding, bounded queue replay, and failure handling.
exclusions: No bashsyslogd run invocation: the task excludes daemon operation in this environment.
No AF_UNIX or UDP traffic, signal delivery, host service interaction, privileged action, or failure-injection shim was executed.
There is no equivalent-output GNU syslogd oracle for this loadable; deferred cases require a disposable VM or reviewed private mocks.

cases.purpose: Verify bashsyslogd appends records to pre-existing private log files and preserves their modes, then leaves fixture files available for copy/move/removal.
Verify bashsyslogd output routing through private hardlink aliases and relative symlinks, with exact record multiplicity and final link identity.
Use Bash's type builtin to verify that the exact candidate registers bashsyslogd as a shell builtin, without invoking its service operation.

Check Bash help output against the pinned documented interface: forwarding target syntax, queue limit, --once, and the AF_UNIX datagram receiver description. The fixed marker is emitted only when all contract tokens are present.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help bashsyslogd)
if [[ $(type -t bashsyslogd) == builtin && $help_text == *"--forward"* && $help_text == *"HOST:PORT"* && $help_text == *"--queue-max-bytes"* && $help_text == *"--once"* && $help_text == *"AF_UNIX"* && $help_text == *"SOCK_DGRAM"* ]]; then
  printf 'help-contract-ok\n'
else
  exit 1
fi
